articles.title: Conditions remain 'unchanged' for young people with disability, data reveal
articles.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
articles.summary: The level of inequity experienced by young people with disability has remained largely unchanged since the turn of the century, according to new research led by Flinders University. Using data from the Household, Income and Labor Dynamics in Australia Survey (HILDA), researchers examined the extent of social inequity experienced by young people ages 15–29 with disability, compared with those without disability, between 2001 and 2023.

articles.title: JWST captures rare glimpse of early black hole growing inside network of young galaxies
articles.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
articles.summary: Astronomers using the James Webb Space Telescope have captured one of the clearest views yet of how an early supermassive black hole may grow within a network of young galaxies. The compact active galaxy, seen just a billion years after the Big Bang, lies beside a 12,000-parsec-long filament containing multiple galaxies that are expected to merge within a few hundred million years.

articles.title: The human side of animal health: Global review reveals new insights to achieving better biosecurity
articles.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
articles.summary: When it comes to protecting livestock from devastating diseases, simply telling people what to do may not be enough. A new review led by a researcher from the University of Vermont and collaborators from two institutions in Australia suggests that improving farm biosecurity requires something often overlooked in animal health: understanding how humans make decisions.

articles.title: A strange quantum effect dramatically boosts energy transfer
articles.summary: Researchers discovered a proton-assisted mechanism that greatly improves how triplet energy moves between quantum dots and nearby molecules. The proton briefly shifts position, helps coordinate electron movement, and then returns to where it started. This quantum-driven shuttle could offer a powerful new way to tune solar cells, lasers, and catalytic reactions.

articles.title: Scientists revive a powerful antibiotic that superbugs had defeated
articles.summary: Scientists have found a way to revive vancomycin, a powerful antibiotic that some dangerous bacteria have learned to resist. Instead of creating an entirely new drug, researchers paired vancomycin with a small molecule called pghi-4, which blocks a bacterial enzyme linked to resistance. The combination restored the antibiotic’s ability to kill drug-resistant E. faecium, raising hopes that similar chemical helpers could rescue other failing medicines.
